ma_pusherman_wall.blurb: Pusherman Wall is one of the busier clusters of boulders in the Temple Area at Hammond Pond, a wooded patch of conservation land on the edge of Boston. The rock is dark puddingstone conglomerate, and the climbing is short and technical, mostly vertical faces. Most problems are in the easy to moderate range, with a handful of harder ones, and a few lines are usually climbed on a top rope. The crags here are a local scene rather than a destination, so bring pads and look hard at the landings before leaving the ground.
ma_pusherman_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the Chestnut Hill shopping center and walk up Hammond Pond Parkway to the former temple building. The conservation land starts just beyond that property, and a short trail leads to the boulders.

mi_freeman_landing.blurb: Freeman Landing is a string of boulder clusters strung along a rocky Lake Superior shoreline trail north of Marquette. The setting is wild and open, with lake breeze, wooded stretches and wide water views. Problems run from the easiest grades up through the mid range, with a few tall, serious lines that need several pads. The footing on the trail is uneven, so wear sturdy shoes. Late spring through early fall suits it best, and lake moisture can leave the rock slick after rain.
mi_freeman_landing.parking_note: Use the Wetmore Landing lot off County Road 550 north of Marquette.
mi_freeman_landing.approach: From the lot, head toward the water. A little before the sand, take the left-hand path out onto the point, then follow the shoreline trail as it curves left. The boulder clusters sit close together along it.

_expect.name: Sand Point Road to Miners Castle

mi_sand_point_road_to_miners_castle.blurb: This stretch of the Pictured Rocks shoreline near Munising holds the most approachable water ice in the Upper Peninsula. Water seeps through the porous sandstone cliffs and freezes into curtains and pillars, most of them moderate, around WI3 and WI4, with a few at WI2 and a few harder. Walks are short, which makes it a good place for newer ice climbers or a quick day. Ice usually builds by late December, and cold, lake-driven weather can change conditions quickly.
mi_sand_point_road_to_miners_castle.parking_note: Take Sand Point Road east out of Munising, past the hospital, to its end at the beach and boat launch.
mi_sand_point_road_to_miners_castle.approach: From the road's end, walk back toward town for about ten minutes to reach the Curtains and the Dryer Hose area. Other formations are reached on the North Country Trail running from the lot.

mi_little_presque_isle.blurb: Little Presque Isle is a wild stretch of Lake Superior shoreline north of Marquette, with beaches, forested dunes and bedrock cliffs and ledges along the water. The bouldering is lakeside, and most problems fall between the easiest grades and V3, with a few harder. Some lines are deep water solos over the lake, so conditions and water depth matter. A handful of roped lines and winter ice formations also sit along the shore. Expect a quiet, scenic outing rather than a big concentration of problems.

mi_slugg_s_bluff_roped.blurb: Slugg's Bluff is a quartzite cliff of roughly 80 feet above the small town of Palmer, about half an hour from Marquette. It offers a good mix of sport routes and gear-protected lines, many of them following cracks, spread from easy climbs through the 5.12 range with the greatest concentration at 5.8 to 5.11. The view across the surrounding country is wide. The cliff is a community favorite for local climbers and is kept up by volunteers.
mi_slugg_s_bluff_roped.parking_note: Drive Anderson Road out of Palmer. A wide spot near the remains of an old house is the usual place to leave the car, and a faint trail climbs from there to the base of the cliff.

mi_north_boulders.blurb: North Boulders is a group of boulders scattered along a powerline cut near Iron Mountain in the Carney area. Slabs are a specialty, including a main slab you can see from the road. Most problems are easy to moderate, between the easiest grades and V2, with a few reaching V4 and V6. The area is still being explored, so more problems turn up in the woods on either side of the cut. Most developed problems are within about ten minutes of the car.
mi_north_boulders.parking_note: Reached from Carney Lake Road, where the powerline crosses.
mi_north_boulders.approach: Follow the powerline cut from where you left the car to the main slab. Further problems lie west of the slab, along the cut to the north, and in the woods on both sides.

mi_cliff_drive_roped.blurb: Cliff Drive is the main roped climbing area of the Keweenaw, a set of quiet, wooded outcrops up to well over a hundred feet tall near Ahmeek. Most of the climbing is gear-protected, with some top-rope and a few sport lines, and the grades lean toward the 5.7 to 5.9 range, making it a good place to learn alongside a few harder lines. Some approaches are overgrown from light traffic. Cracks can seep for a while after rain, and fall color is a highlight.
mi_cliff_drive_roped.approach: Walks range from roughly 15 to 40 minutes depending on whether you are heading to the base or the top of a cliff.

mi_carney_crag.blurb: Carney Crag is a small crag in state forest near Iron Mountain, close to the Wisconsin line, reached by a pleasant walk through the woods. Sport routes dominate, with a smaller number of trad lines and top-ropes and a few boulder problems. Most of the routes fall between 5.6 and 5.10, with a few harder ones, and good holds make it a friendly place for newer leaders. Another crag nearby gives a backup on busy days.

mi_beach_side.blurb: Beach Side is a shoreline cluster of boulders on Lake Superior at the Wetmore Landing end of the bouldering north of Marquette. Problems are mostly low-grade, with a lot of the easiest grades and V0, and a few going to V5 and above, so it suits warm-ups and beginners. Footing is rocky and uneven, and lake moisture can leave the rock slick after rain. Late spring through early fall is the usual window.
mi_beach_side.parking_note: Start from the Wetmore Landing lot off County Road 550 north of Marquette.

mi_sunset_gully.blurb: Sunset Gully is a crag on the slopes of Sugarloaf Mountain north of Marquette, popular with Upper Peninsula climbers for its wide spread of difficulty and as a place to learn. Climbing is mostly sport and top-rope, with a few trad lines and a number of boulder problems, from beginner routes through the 5.12 range. You share the trailhead with hikers and walk through the woods to the cliff. Ledges and slabs can turn slick after wet weather.
